limitations.statement: The implementation and guarantee require exact proximal operations and a supplied valid global Lipschitz constant; they do not bound the internal computational cost of either acquisition.
No unrestricted Oracle Complexity lower bound, iterate-convergence claim, support restriction, or guarantee for inexact/stochastic/nonconvex variants is extracted here.

performance_links.scope_note: Theorem 4.4, alpha=1, under the complete assumptions in the linked record.

variants.cost: Per iteration: one exact gradient evaluation, one exact proximal minimization for g/L, scalar arithmetic and O(n) vector arithmetic; constant many n-vectors suffice. K iterations charge K gradient evaluations and K proximal operations separately. Function values are not required by this fixed-step update. Obtaining a valid L and implementing the proximal operation have problem-dependent costs not bounded here; a proximal operation is not a free gradient query.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Section 4 constant-step box, printed p.193/PDF p.11, (4.1)–(4.3); p_L definition printed p.189/PDF p.7, (2.5)–(2.6).
variants.name: Constant-step FISTA
variants.output: Return x_K, the final proximal iterate, for a finite-budget run; the stated guarantee concerns x_k, not the extrapolated point y_k.
public_inputs: Functions f,g on R^n under the stated requirements.
Known L=L(f)>0 satisfying ||∇f(x)−∇f(y)||≤L||x−y|| for every x,y; L need not be the smallest valid constant.
Initial point x_0 in R^n and, for a finite run, an integer iteration budget K≥1.
variants.query_and_update: At iteration k≥1 query ∇f(y_k), set z_k=y_k−∇f(y_k)/L, and obtain x_k=argmin_x {g(x)+(L/2)||x−z_k||²}. Set t_{k+1}=(1+sqrt(1+4t_k²))/2 and y_{k+1}=x_k+((t_k−1)/t_{k+1})(x_k−x_{k−1}). This is p_L(y_k) in (2.6).
variants.requirements: n is a positive finite integer. f:R^n→R is convex C^1 with global L-Lipschitz gradient; g:R^n→R is continuous convex, possibly nonsmooth; argmin(f+g) is nonempty. Exact gradient and exact proximal minimization are available. Norm is Euclidean.
variants.state_and_initialization: Store consecutive x iterates, y_k and scalar t_k. Set y_1=x_0 and t_1=1.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Use the fixed supplied L, giving forward step 1/L; no line search. The source defines an indefinitely indexed sequence. For a finite-budget execution perform k=1,…,K; this stopping convention introduces no additional convergence claim. No computable objective-gap stopping certificate is supplied by the algorithm box.

use_restrictions: Resource accounting counts exact proximal operations separately from gradients; it is an implementation accounting of the displayed rule, not an unrestricted Oracle Complexity result.
The finite-budget output convention is explicit; no source-supplied automatic stopping certificate is claimed.
